_comment: DreamRehearse SIM assets. PROVENANCE. Every clip is re-encoded from a private Hugging Face dataset under hchen657Naza/ (robotwin_dream_success_videos is public); each row carries _source_path with the exact repo-relative path(s) it came from, and _episode with the source episode identifier. TRIM/SCALE: nothing was trimmed and nothing was scaled. Every source clip is natively 640x480, every row's cells already agreed on decoded frame count and fps, so all 30 outputs are 640x480 at the source's own frame count. Frame counts and fps in this file come from decoding each output file (ffprobe -count_frames), not from container metadata. Output timestamps were rewritten with setpts=N/(fps*TB) so each row is exactly constant-rate and plays in lockstep; no frame was dropped or duplicated. SKELETON MATCHING: see meta.skeleton_matching. Six training rows include one deliberate 'failed' episode because the 8-task training set is roughly a third failures by design and hiding that would misrepresent it.

sources.hchen657Naza/wm_8tasks_training_dataset: RoboTwin 2.0, aloha-agilex bimanual, Wide_D435 head camera fovy 55. 490 clip pairs over 8 tasks, each task split success/ and failed/ (320 success, 170 failed). <prefix>_rgb.mp4 is the prediction target, <prefix>_skeleton.mp4 the FK projection of the commanded 14-D joint targets. NOTE: the files decode as 640x480 at 30 fps, while the repo README states '480x640, 15 fps' - the fps in the README is wrong.
sources.hchen657Naza/egovla_wm_data: EgoBench / EgoVLA ego-humanoid: Unitree H1 + Inspire dex hands in Isaac Sim, fixed top camera, 640x480 at 15 fps. Open-Drawer / Stack-Can / Unload-Cans carry 50 success + 30 failed each with skeletons. Close-Drawer is listed in the repo but has only 5 episodes, is 224x224, and ships NO skeleton video, so it cannot form a pair; it was not used. Every episode in the repo is from one room (room 1 / table 1).
sources.hchen657Naza/abc55_skeleton_wm: Derived subset of xdof/ABC-130k: real bimanual YAM retail stations, 1623 episodes over 55 tasks, 640x480 at 30 fps, rgb.mp4 + rendered skeleton.mp4 + actions.npz. Episodes are long (mean ~81 s); the one used here is among the shortest. 'success/' is nominal, not a verified outcome. skeleton.mp4 ships as MPEG-4 and was re-encoded to H.264.
sources.hchen657Naza/robotwin_data: RoboTwin ACT rollout collections, 640x480 at 30 fps. Two trees: robotwin_wm_data/<task>/{success,failure}/<ep>/ and act_rollouts_4new/<seed>/<task>/{success,failure}/<ep>/. Each episode holds rgb.mp4, skeleton.mp4, overlay.mp4, actions.npz and, for most tasks, rgb_left_wrist.mp4 / rgb_right_wrist.mp4 as well.
sources.hchen657Naza/egovla_dream_success_videos: 894 closed-loop EgoVLA dreams whose actions succeeded in Isaac Sim, over 4 tasks x rooms r2t2/r4t4/r5t5, 640x480 at 15 fps. Per episode: dream.mp4 (generated), sim.mp4 (the simulator's render of the same actions = ground truth), side_by_side.mp4 (dream | sim | conditioning skeleton), actions.npz, robometer.json, meta.json. The <task>/r1t1/ directories are NOT dreams - they are 229 ground-truth simulator demos with sim.mp4 only - and were not used for fidelity rows.
sources.hchen657Naza/robotwin_dream_success_vide: PUBLIC. 1842 RoboTwin dreams kept by a Robometer threshold, <task>/<clean|noisy>/setN/episode_N/, 640x480 at 30 fps. Per episode: dream.mp4, side_by_side.mp4 (GT | dream | skeleton), actions.npz and usually ee_pose.npz. There is NO standalone ground-truth video, so the GT cell here is the first panel of side_by_side.mp4. 77 of the 1842 episodes have no side_by_side.mp4 at all and cannot be used for a GT comparison.

meta.encode: H.264 libx264, preset slow, crf 23, yuv420p, profile high level 4.0, -movflags +faststart, no audio. No scaling and no trimming: all 30 clips are 640x480 at their source frame count. Timestamps rewritten with setpts=N/(fps*TB) and muxed with -fps_mode passthrough so each clip is exactly 15/1 or 30/1 fps with every decoded source frame preserved. Encoded on CPU (the node's GPUs hold resident world-model servers and were left alone). Per-row frame counts were verified by decoding (ffprobe -count_frames) after encoding, not from container metadata. 30 files, 12800628 bytes total, largest 1074824 bytes.
meta.skeleton_matching: RESOLVED, and every fidelity row has a genuine same-episode skeleton. The route is NOT a cross-repo match - it is that both dream repos ship the conditioning skeleton inside side_by_side.mp4, as the third panel of a 1920x480 composite with the same decoded frame count and fps as dream.mp4 and sim.mp4. Panel identity was verified by PSNR on all four egovla tasks: panel 0 scores 48.7-50.2 dB against dream.mp4, panel 1 scores 50.9-52.8 dB against sim.mp4, and panel 2 is black-background line art (mean luma 1.3-1.4). For RoboTwin, panel 1 scores 44.6 dB against dream.mp4 and panel 0 only 23.6 dB, confirming the README's GT | dream | skeleton order. Because the skeleton is the same file, the same frame index and the same episode as the dream, there is no substitution and no alignment guesswork. WHAT DOES NOT WORK: egovla_dream_success_videos episodes cannot be matched to egovla_wm_data skeletons, and no such match was attempted. (1) No recorded link: meta.json carries task, room_idx, table_idx, source_episode, scene_init_i, policy, world_model and chunking, and actions.npz carries actions/qpos/ee/hand/chunk_taus/init_i/vla_ckpt/wm_port - neither has any field naming a skeleton file or an egovla_wm_data episode. (2) Different rooms: every egovla_wm_data episode is room 1 / table 1, while the dreams used here are rooms 2, 4 and 5. (3) Different policies: egovla_wm_data skeletons come from ACT rollouts (with injected noise for the failures), the dreams from EgoVLA ckpt-6720 acting on imagined frames, so the action sequences differ by construction. (4) Different indexing: egovla_wm_data runs ep000-ep049 per task, while dream episode_N is the source scene index and reaches 142. (5) Measured: the r2t2/episode_34 skeleton panel scores 25.2 dB against egovla_wm_data Open-Drawer ep000 and ep001 skeletons, versus 50.4 dB against its own side_by_side panel. OPTION NOT TAKEN: a skeleton could in principle be rendered from a dream episode's actions.npz - its actions (T,38) = [left_ee pos+quat 7 | right_ee 7 | left_hand 12 | right_hand 12] is exactly the commanded ee_pose + finger qpos convention that egovla_wm_data says its analytical skeletons are FK'd from - but no renderer was built, and none is needed because side_by_side.mp4 already carries the real conditioning skeleton.
meta.robometer: Fidelity rows from egovla_dream_success_videos carry the episode's raw Robometer-4B scores. Robometer-4B was run with --fps 3 --max-frames 16, i.e. 16 frames spread over the whole clip. Three scorings per episode: dream_video_config_prompt (the dream, scored against the task's collection-config prompt), dream_video_wm_caption (the dream, scored against the world model's training caption), sim_video_config_prompt (the simulator render, config prompt). Within each, prog_* are progress-head scores and succ_* are success-head scores; peak is the max over the 16 sampled frames, final the last, mean the average, succ_peak_frame the index of the peak among those 16. The 16-point per-frame progress_curve / success_curve arrays were left out of this file for size; they are in each episode's robometer.json. THESE ARE SCORES, NOT A VERDICT. Do not render them as success or failure: on generated frames Robometer separates sim-success from sim-failure only weakly (AUC 0.60-0.75 on dreams, versus 0.99+ on the simulator renders), and it systematically under-detects success on dreams for some tasks and over-detects it for others.
meta.excluded: The abc55_skeleton_wm (ABC-130k, real bimanual station) row was removed at the owner's request: this section covers the EgoBench and RoboTwin embodiments only.
